description: Ask someone what their hobby or interests are. It works in casual and polite spe

examples.en: What are your hobbies?
What are your hobbies, oppa?
What are your hobbies? Mine is photography!

description: Quickly agree by saying you feel the same way. It works in casual and polite spe

examples.en: Me too! I love K-pop too!
Me too — it's really delicious!
Me too! Let's go together!

description: Say something is not great or doesn't meet expectations. Say what you need, then

examples.en: I don't really like spicy food.
I don't really like this style.
This drama isn't really my thing.

description: Invite someone to take a photo together. Just place a noun before 같이 사진 찍어요 — no

examples.en: Let's take a photo together!
Let's take a photo together in front of Gyeongbokgung!
Let's take a photo here together!

description: Ask if the photo turned out well. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Co

examples.en: Did the photo turn out well?
Did the selfie turn out well?
The photo turned out great — you look pretty!

description: Ask someone how they've been doing. Just place a noun before 잘 지냈어요 — no conjuga

examples.en: Have you been well?
Have you been well lately?
Have you been well? Were you very busy?

description: Casually ask how something was. Just place a noun before 어땠어 — no conjugation ne

examples.en: How was the Han River?
How was the exam?
How was the first day?

description: Say 'it was my first time, but...' to describe a new experience. It works in cas

examples.en: It was my first time, but it was really delicious!
It was my first time, but it was easier than I thought.
It was my first time, but I want to go again!

description: Softly express a guess or opinion with 'I think' or 'it seems.' Say what you nee

examples.en: It seems like it'll be delicious!
It seems like it'll be difficult.
It seems like it's famous.

description: Make a casual inference: 'it seems like' or 'I guess.' Say what you need, then a

examples.en: It must be delicious — the line is long!
It must be famous.
They must be busy.

description: Say you have to or must do something. Just place a noun before 해야 해 — no conjuga

examples.en: You have to study now!
You have to eat.
You absolutely have to go!

description: Tell someone not to do something, casually. Just place a noun before 하지 마 — no c

examples.en: Don't worry!
Don't be late!
Don't give up!

description: Ask for someone's opinion on a specific topic. Say what you need, then add 어떻게 생

examples.en: What do you think about Korean food?
What do you think about this drama?
What do you think about my idea?

description: Agree with and validate what someone just said. It works in casual and polite sp

examples.en: That's a good point. I think so too.
That's a good point, but I see it differently.
That's a valid point!

description: Politely say you're a bit different or have your own preference. It works in cas

examples.en: I'm a bit different — I love spicy food!
examples.ko: 저는 좀 달라요, 매운 거 좋아해요!

examples.en: I'm a bit different — I prefer bands.
examples.ko: 저는 좀 달라요, 밴드가 더 좋아요.

examples.en: My taste is a bit different.

description: Ask if someone has ever visited a particular place. Just place a noun before 에 가

examples.en: Have you been to Jeju Island?
Have you been to Gyeongbokgung?
Have you been to Busan?

description: Strongly recommend that someone visit a place. Say what you need, then add 꼭 가 보

examples.en: You should definitely visit the Han River!
You should definitely check out Gwangjang Market!
You should definitely go to Jeju Island!

description: Ask what shows or content someone is watching these days. It works in casual and

examples.en: What are you watching lately?
What dramas are you watching lately?
What are you watching lately? Give me a recommendation!

description: Say you're totally hooked or obsessed with something. Say what you need, then ad

examples.en: I'm totally hooked on this drama!
I'm totally hooked on K-pop!
I'm totally absorbed in studying Korean.

description: Express excitement and anticipation for the next episode. It works in casual and

examples.en: I can't wait for the next episode!
I can't wait for next week!
I can't wait to see the ending!

description: Ask if someone knows or recognizes a particular song. It works in casual and pol

examples.en: Do you know this song?
Do you know this song? I love it so much!
Do you know New Jeans' songs?

description: Ask what a song's lyrics mean. Say what you need, then add 가사가 무슨 뜻이에요 at the en

examples.en: What does this lyric mean?
What does '그리워' mean?
What does this part of the lyrics mean?

description: Ask if something actually works or makes a difference. Say what you need, then a

examples.en: Is this serum effective?
Does this diet method work?
Does this medicine work?

description: Say the reviews or word-of-mouth for something are great. Say what you need, the

examples.en: The reviews for this cream are amazing!
This restaurant has great reviews — let's go!
I bought it because the reviews were good.

description: Ask how often someone does a particular activity. Just place a noun before 얼마나 자

examples.en: How often do you exercise?
How often do you go to cafés?
How often do you study Korean?

description: Say that something is good for your health. Just place a noun before 건강에 좋아요 — n

examples.en: Walking is good for your health!
Kimchi is good for your health.
Sleeping well is good for your health.
examples.ko: 잠 잘 자는 게 건강에 좋아요.

description: Ask where someone currently lives. Just place a noun before 어디 살아요 — no conjugat

examples.en: Where in Korea do you live?
Where in Seoul do you live?
Where are you living now?
